binders: n is an arbitrary natural number, with n = 0 allowed.
A, L, U, factorError, lowerError, and upperError are arbitrary real n-by-n matrices.
v, y, computed, rhsLower, and rhsUpper are arbitrary real n-vectors.
xi, epsilon, gammaP, gammaC, and factorRemainder are arbitrary real numbers.
mathematical_definitions: DeltaA is the explicitly computed matrix ((factorError + lowerError*U) + L*upperError) + lowerError*upperError.
DeltaRhs is the explicitly computed vector (rhsLower + L*rhsUpper) + lowerError*rhsUpper.
Matrix multiplication is (B*C)_{ij} = sum_k B_{ik}C_{kj}, with k ranging over all indices in Fin n.
Matrix-vector multiplication is (B*x)_i = sum_j B_{ij}x_j, with j ranging over all indices in Fin n.
||B||_F is the Frobenius norm of a real matrix B.
||x||_2 = sqrt(sum_i x_i^2) is the Euclidean norm of a real vector x.
All matrix and vector additions are pointwise.
No existential witnesses occur: DeltaA and DeltaRhs are fixed expressions determined by the universally quantified inputs.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every dimension n, square real matrices A, L, U and three matrix errors, real n-vectors v, y, computed and two right-hand-side errors, and real scalars xi, epsilon, gammaP, gammaC, and factorRemainder, assume 0 <= gammaP < 1 and gammaC >= 0. Assume LU equals A plus factorError, that y solves the perturbed lower system (L+lowerError)y = v+rhsLower, and that computed solves the perturbed upper system (U+upperError)computed = y+rhsUpper. Assume the five stated Frobenius- and Euclidean-norm bounds on these errors. Then computed exactly satisfies the single perturbed system (A+DeltaA)computed = v+DeltaRhs, where DeltaA = factorError+lowerError*U+L*upperError+lowerError*upperError and DeltaRhs = rhsLower+L*rhsUpper+lowerError*rhsUpper, with the displayed exact parenthesizations. Moreover, DeltaA and DeltaRhs obey the two stated norm bounds, including respectively the coefficient 3*gammaC+gammaC^2 and the coefficient gammaP*(1+gammaC)^2/(1-gammaP).

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The dimension n need not be positive. For n = 0, all matrices and vectors have empty index sets and all corresponding finite sums and norms are zero, so the statement has a degenerate zero-dimensional case.
The theorem is universally quantified and conditional; whenever any hypothesis is inconsistent with the chosen data, the implication is vacuously true.
Only gammaP and gammaC have sign restrictions: 0 <= gammaP < 1 and gammaC >= 0. There is no upper bound on gammaC.
xi, epsilon, and factorRemainder have no nonnegativity or size assumptions. In particular, the names do not encode that epsilon is a machine precision or that factorRemainder is nonnegative.
The condition gammaP < 1 ensures 1-gammaP > 0, so the denominator in the final bound is nonzero and positive.
There are no invertibility, nonsingularity, conditioning, or rank assumptions on A, L, or U.
Despite their names, L and U are not required to be lower- or upper-triangular, and lowerError and upperError have no triangularity or sparsity constraints.
The proposition does not assert existence or uniqueness of y or computed; it applies to arbitrary vectors satisfying the assumed equations.
The perturbations in the conclusion are not existentially chosen or optimized. They are the exact aggregate expressions DeltaA and DeltaRhs.
All arithmetic is exact real arithmetic. No floating-point datatype, rounding operation, probabilistic model, componentwise error model, or computational algorithm is encoded.
The error controls are normwise only: Frobenius norm for matrices and Euclidean norm for vectors.
No semantic interpretation of xi, epsilon, gammaP, gammaC, or factorRemainder beyond their occurrences in the displayed assumptions and conclusions is encoded.
